request.prompt: Which humanoid robots are suitable for research?

result.text:
Choosing the right humanoid robot for research depends heavily on your budget, whether you are studying bipedal locomotion, AI/manipulation, or human-robot interaction, and how much open-source software access you need.

Several prominent platforms stand out across different research tiers:

1. Entry-Level & Value Research

Unitree G1 EDU: Widely considered one of the best-value entry points into bipedal and manipulation research. While the consumer base model is inexpensive, the EDU version unlocks open APIs, secondary development, and seamless integration with ROS/ROS 2, Python, C++, and Linux.

Booster Robotics T1 / K1: Built explicitly as research and training platforms, featuring high degrees of freedom (DoF) and out-of-the-box ROS 2 compatibility, open APIs, and simulation support.

2. Full-Size Bipedal & Whole-Body Manipulation

Fourier GR Series (GR-1 / GR-2): Popular for academic and lab trials involving whole-body movement, heavy-duty actuators, and complex grasping. The GR-2 scales up degrees of freedom (~53 DoF) making it well-suited for full-scale human-mimetic physical tasks.

Apptronik Apollo: Built with a heavy focus on industrial AI training and modularity, making it ideal for labs bridging the gap between academic reinforcement learning and real-world warehouse/factory logistics.

Boston Dynamics Atlas (Electric): Featuring high degrees of freedom, extreme payload capacity, and rugged build quality, Atlas is the gold standard for high-end industrial and dynamic physics research—though typically accessible primarily to well-funded partner labs.

3. Human-Robot Interaction & Social/Service Research

PAL Robotics ARI / TIAGo: If your research centers on human-robot interaction (HRI), social behavior, or mobile manipulation rather than human-like bipedal walking, platforms like ARI or TIAGo are deeply integrated with ROS/ROS 2. They save labs from the constant maintenance and safety hurdles of balancing a bipedal robot.

Key Questions to Narrow Down Your Choice:

Locomotion or Manipulation? Do you strictly need a bipedal walking robot, or will a wheeled/torso-based mobile manipulator suffice?

Software Stack: Does your team require full open-source access (ROS 2, custom C++/Python control loops), or a closed/semi-closed ecosystem?

Budget Scale: Are you working with an entry academic grant ($15k–$40k range like Unitree) or a multi-hundred-thousand-dollar institutional lab budget?

If you can share what specific research domain you're focusing on (e.g., reinforcement learning for walking, fine-dexterity hand manipulation, or human-robot social interaction) and your approximate budget, I can give you a targeted shortlist and compare their software ecosystems.
